newsitem.title: USA: Clinton taps Green Beret to be top U.S. officer.
newsitem.headline: Clinton taps Green Beret to be top U.S. officer.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Thursday named Army Gen. Henry Shelton, a Green Beret paratrooper who led U.S. forces in Haiti, to be chairman of the military Joint Chiefs of Staff.

In announcing his selection of the 55-year old special forces commander to be the top officer in the armed forces, Clinton said Shelton brought "unique perspective" to the job because because of his expertise in unconventional warfare.

"Over more than three decades of service to our nation, he (Shelton) has distinguished himself as a decorated soldier, an innovative thinker, a superb commander. From Vietnam to Desert Storm, he has proven his skill and courage in combat," Clinton said at a White House Rose Garden ceremony.

The president added that Shelton's extensive experience in joint military operations and building coalitions with other nations "give him invaluable tools to serve as chairman in our more interdependent world."

If approved by the Senate to succeed Army Gen. John Shalikashvili, who will retire from the military at the end of September, Shelton would jump from leading elite commando forces in the U.S. Special Operations Command to being top man at the Pentagon.

The selection of the 34-year veteran of military service apparently ends a long search for a successor to Shalikashvili that was complicated after Air Force Gen Joseph Ralston -- Defence Secretary William Cohen's first choice for the post -- withdrew from consideration after an adulterous affair in his background came to light.
